- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in early days of the 30d horizon — model reacts slowly to recent price drops or spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction for sudden sentiment shifts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward adjustments to prevent excessive sell-off in forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with the dominant sentiment trend; align forecast mean to recent 5–7 day sentiment-weighted average.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 10–15 days of forecast if sentiment is bullish.
